**What shipped.** One helper pair (`jobs/localtime.sh` / `localtime.py`) with the zone name on exactly one line, Python parsing it out of the shell file so the halves can't drift. Display sites converted and always carrying the zone; data sites left UTC with a one-line reason at each, guarded by the selftest so deleting a reason turns the gate red.

**The four things worth carrying forward**, all measured rather than argued:

1. `Pacific/Los_Angeles` isn't a zone. The brief's literal helper would have printed `13:40 Pacific` for `06:40 PDT` — UTC wearing a converted-looking label, worse than leaving UTC. The check asks what a silent fallback can't fake: non-zero offset, and an abbreviation that differs between July and January.
2. The host was already Pacific, so `nightly_build.sh` was applying the correction twice by being local and unlabelled.
3. `summarise_run.py`'s `ts` is the left side of a lexical `awk '$1 >= c'`, not a display field. Converting it would have silently dropped rows.
4. My own: an unguarded import in `fleet.py` killed ten unrelated checks, because `selftest.d/93` runs that file from a three-file copy. Guarded, degrading to UTC *labelled UTC* — a fallback saying `PDT` while on UTC would have reintroduced finding #1 inside its own fix.

The rule left in NOTES for the next lane: **convert at the point of printing, never at the point of storing — a stored field is somebody's sort key.**

Two reversible judgement calls are flagged in the PR body: the `fleet.py` generated-at line (it had no absolute time to convert) and `cloud.sh`'s audit filename moving to local (`date -u +%F` past 17:00 Pacific was filing Tuesday's audit under Wednesday). I also left a note that `selftest.d/60-status.sh` — not my file — hardcodes fixture rows dated `2026-09-19T01:00:00Z` inside a 24-hour window, so it expires tomorrow and will fail for an unrelated reason.
